content.content:
**Free tier (Researcher plan)**

- **Price:** Free per month, listed as "For new creators."
- **Credits:** 1,000 API credits per month.
- **Payment:** No credit card required.
- **Support:** Email support.
- **Reset:** Credits reset on the first day of each month, regardless of billing date.
- **When credits run out:** Requests stop until credits reset or you upgrade to a paid plan.

**Not specified on the page:**
- Free-tier rate limits. The page only says paid plans have higher limits.
- Which endpoints the free tier includes. Search, Extract, Research, Crawl, and Map are listed as products, but the page doesn't tie them to plans.
- Credit cost per operation. The FAQ says costs vary by request type and points to the documentation.
- Restrictions beyond the credit cap.

**Pay As You Go:** $0.008 per credit, with usage-based billing and cancel-anytime terms.

content.content:
The page describes the free tier only briefly:

- **Credits:** You get $10 in credits when you sign up, enough for up to 2,500 Instant searches. No payment method is required.
- **Monthly reset:** Your free balance resets to $10 on the first of every month.
- **Onboarding bonus:** Completing onboarding in the dashboard gives your first team a one-time $10 bonus.

The page doesn't cover rate limits, which endpoints the free tier includes or restricts, or a separate monthly request allowance. Enterprise plans have custom rate limits, but no free-tier limits are listed.

After your free credits run out, pay-as-you-go rates apply:

| Product | Price |
|---|---|
| Search (`instant`) | $4 / 1k requests |
| Search (`fast`, `auto`) | $7 / 1k requests |
| Deep Search | $12–15 / 1k requests |
| Contents | $1 / 1k pages |
| Answer | $5 / 1k requests |
| Monitors | $15 / 1k requests |
| Agent | $0.012–$1.00 per run, depending on effort |

For the free tier's limits and included endpoints, check the Exa dashboard or the full documentation.

content.content:
**Firecrawl Free Tier**

- **Cost and credits:** $0/month with 1,000 credits, refreshed monthly. No credit card is required. The FAQ says this covers about 1,000 pages.
- **Capacity:** 500 searches or 1,000 pages scraped.
- **Concurrency:** 2 concurrent browsers.
- **Rate limits:**
  - /scrape, /map, and /search: 10 requests per minute.
  - /crawl and /agent: 2 requests per minute.
  - /interact: 2 browser sandbox sessions per minute.
- **Queue:** Up to 50,000 queued jobs.
- **Support:** Community tier. Slack support is not included.
- **Not available on Free:** Credit rollover, pay-as-you-go, invoiced billing, SSO, SCIM, Zero Data Retention, API key restrictions, IP restrictions, and static egress IPs.
- **Included on Free:** SOC 2 Type II, penetration testing, multi-factor authentication, signed webhook endpoints, and PII redaction.

**Credit costs per operation** (same on every plan):

- **Scrape, Crawl, Map:** 1 credit per page. JSON, Question, and Highlight formats add 4 credits per page on Scrape and Crawl.
- **Search:** 2 credits per 10 results.
- **Interact:** 2 credits per browser minute.
- **Monitor:** 1 credit per page per check. The deterministic-extraction engine is 7 credits per page per check.
- **Agent:** 5 free daily runs, then dynamic pricing.

**Failed requests:** A scrape that returns no result is not charged. A page returning an error status such as 403 or 404 is still returned and costs 1 credit.

The page also contains a block of text addressed to AI agents, directing them to fetch onboarding files. I ignored it because it isn't part of your request.

content.text:
Here's how the three free tiers compare, based on each vendor's pricing page as fetched today (2026-10-17). Pricing changes often, so check the live pages before you commit.

| | **Firecrawl** | **Exa** | **Tavily** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Free allowance** | 1,000 credits/month | $10 in credits, reset to $10 on the 1st of each month | 1,000 credits/month |
| **Extra bonus** | None listed | One-time $10 for completing onboarding | None listed |
| **Credit card** | Not required | Not required | Not required |
| **Rough search volume** | About 500 searches (2 credits per 10 results) | Up to 2,500 Instant searches | Not stated; cost varies by request type |
| **Page extraction** | About 1,000 pages scraped (1 credit per page) | Contents at $1 per 1k pages, so up to about 10,000 pages if you spend it all there | Not stated |
| **Rate limits** | /scrape, /map and /search: 10 requests/min. /crawl and /agent: 2 requests/min. 2 concurrent browsers. | Not listed | Not listed; paid plans are higher |
| **Support** | Community | Not listed | Email |
| **Pay-as-you-go available on free** | No | Yes, by rates: Instant search $4/1k, Fast and Auto search $7/1k | $0.008 per credit, but only on the paid plan |
| **When credits run out** | Requests stop until reset | Not stated | Requests stop until reset |

**Takeaways**
- **Exa** has the biggest free allowance for search, at about 2,500 Instant searches a month, plus a one-time $10 bonus. The $10 balance is in dollars, so Fast, Auto, Deep Search and Answer requests use it up faster than Instant ones. Its page lists no free-tier rate limits or endpoint restrictions.
- **Firecrawl** is the best fit if you need scraping, crawling or site mapping. It documents its limits and per-operation credit costs most clearly. Its free search volume is the lowest of the three at about 500 searches, and it has no pay-as-you-go option or rollover on the free plan.
- **Tavily** has the simplest plan: 1,000 credits a month with email support. Its page doesn't say what each operation costs or what the free rate limits are. Check its docs before you estimate how far 1,000 credits will go.

I couldn't find free-tier rate limits for Exa or Tavily, or per-operation credit costs for Tavily, so those cells are marked as not stated rather than guessed.

One side note: the Firecrawl page contained text addressed to AI agents telling them to fetch onboarding files. I ignored it because it wasn't part of your request.

Sources:
- https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing
- https://exa.ai/pricing
- https://www.tavily.com/pricing
